review.description: Added PAGE-REPORTS, list/detail panes and widget instances, selection/evidence/recovery/refresh connections, and the Reported issues navigation endpoint. Processing, outcome, closure and delivery are distinct. Selected report details remain current across overlapping mutation/journal responses and selection changes. W-REPORT-LIST now declares 14 scoped elements and W-REPORT-DETAIL 32, with canonical glossary references. Query, pagination and external-link connections have explicit owned endpoints. Continuing background list refresh does not disable pagination; only a requested additional page suppresses duplicate page requests.
review.implementation: Read ReportedIssues query pagination, query-owned active guards and coalesced loaded-range refresh, selected-report mutation handling, recovery controls and explicit Unknown/freshness displays. Connections identify actual owned endpoints and new widgets have implementation/assertion mappings. The new destination exposed a 390px overflow regression in existing fixtures; nav flex wrapping restores the asserted viewport width. The existing notice rule now also owns button.notice:hover, preserving its yellow background and brown foreground instead of inheriting the dark generic hover tint. Journal updates replay the loaded page range without cancelling a pending Load more; filter changes replace the query owner and reset pagination. One detail-request generation gates both journal and mutation reads; old-selection mutations exit before changing the current selection generation. Fixture-only port overrides preserve default listeners, strict ownership, health checks and direct-connection protections. Existing connection triggers start at select/add-evidence/resume/refresh elements. C-REPORT-QUERY, C-REPORT-MORE and C-REPORT-OPEN-LINK represent existing interactions. Freshness has its exact helper anchor. Journal detail scheduling coalesces per selection without invalidating a slower pending response; mutation requests retain generation-based stale protection. ReportedIssues keeps its existing single-owner page traversal and loaded range, with a local pending-page guard independent of background refresh. W-REPORT-LIST states and C-REPORT-MORE interactions now state that distinction explicitly. Report mutation refresh promises now settle after their own render; subsequent coalesced journal refreshes run independently in the same local loader. The evidence submission owner now binds an attempt to its submitted text, preserving unchanged retry identity and allowing edited retained drafts to submit distinctly. Rebase preserves all incoming confirmed-question UI states and assertion ownership. Manually merged the independent appended test inventories, then rendered generated references and type-checked combined source; reporting controls remain separately owned.
review.tests: Three browser fixtures assert report selection/search, host evidence and idempotency key, acknowledgement-gated recovery, issue links, unknown/stable/prerelease displays and all structured filters with 30-to-32-row pagination. Installed-host/assistive-technology coverage remains a typed gap. UI-QUESTION-RECOVERY now explicitly hovers the Waiting for your answer notice before the 390px light/dark WCAG scan; this reproduces dark contrast 1.43:1 before the CSS repair and passes in both themes afterward. The pagination fixture deliberately delays the second page through an observed journal cursor update, retains all 32 unique IDs, refreshes later-row text and resets to 30 after clearing filters. The recovery fixture asserts the exact selected issue URL reaches ui/open-link. UI-REPORTS-DETAIL-ORDER delays a mutation detail until newer journal processing/findings/recovery controls render, then proves the old response cannot overwrite them. UI-REPORTS-SELECTION-ORDER delays an old mutation and current selection read, then proves the current detail still arrives. Normal configured ports 43173/43174 pass five reporting and three assembled-daemon tests without stopping another checkout. UI-REPORTS-DETAIL-PROGRESS releases responses only after multiple real journal poll cycles and asserts findings, needs-attention and recovery controls while updates continue. Existing ordering, selection, pagination, exact issue URL and light/dark hover regressions remain. Scoped element and connection tests validate schema and references; typed widget/link gaps explicitly retain untested variants. UI-REPORTS-PAGE-PROGRESS delays cloned responses across six confirmed journal polls, requires enabled pagination during background reads, admits one page from a double click, asserts the exact 60 unique IDs and second-page content, and keeps the button usable through another background pass. The original source fails the enabled assertion; final nine focused browser cases and TypeScript pass. This does not close request-failure, accessibility or installed-host gaps. UI-REPORTS-MUTATION-PROGRESS spans delayed list reads and journal changes, proving actual refresh/evidence/recovery controls usable and a second evidence request delivered before background refresh completes. UI-REPORTS-EVIDENCE-RETRY observes accepted-but-unacknowledged additions, exact unchanged retry identity/no duplicate, and successful edited payload with a fresh identity; other failure/accessibility/host gaps remain explicit. Incoming clarification/nonblocking fixtures and all report fixtures coexist; no upstream UI entity, instance or assertion changed by the target and untouched by reporting was lost.
